ai.title: Simplify base2 system prompt, add Codebuff meta-info
ai.summary: Refactored system prompt in .agents/base2/base2.ts. Removed legacy layering instructions, consolidated mandates, and added Codebuff product context (modes, credits, /usage command). Introduced isSonnet flag to conditionally apply specific response guidelines.

eli5.text: The assistant's instruction manual was rewritten to be shorter and clearer, and it now includes information about the product it works for, including how users can ask about their account usage. A new setting was also added that changes how the assistant behaves when running on a specific model. These changes only affect the internal version used by developers and don't change anything you can do today.

ai.title: base2 prompt tweak: spawn directive removed
ai.summary: Removed unconditional `spawn best-of-n-editor` directive from `buildImplementationStepPrompt` in `.agents/base2/base2.ts`. Added `or until you require more information from the user` termination clause to `isMax` prompt. Affects internal agent orchestration prompts only.

eli5.text: The helpful assistant that works behind the scenes on code now stops itself earlier when it doesn't have enough to go on. Instead of always asking another specialized helper to review its work, it can finish on its own, and it will say so explicitly when it's waiting on you. You won't see this directly, but if you're watching the assistant's progress, you may notice it wrapping up sooner and asking for what it needs, rather than continuing to refine its work.

ai.title: CLI hooks extracted from chat.tsx
ai.summary: Three hooks split out from `chat.tsx`: `use-exit-handler.ts` (CtrlC/SIGINT exit flow with analytics flush), `use-message-virtualization.ts` (windowing logic for 60+ top-level messages), `use-suggestion-menu-handlers.ts` (slash/mention menu key handling). Exit handler tracks `nextCtrlCWillExit` state with 2s timeout; clears input on first CtrlC when text present, flushes analytics before `process.exit(0)` on second. Virtualization hook computes `shouldVirtualize`, `virtualTopLevelMessages`, `hiddenTopLevelCount` from `MAX_VIRTUALIZED_TOP_LEVEL=60` and `VIRTUAL_OVERSCAN=12`. Suggestion menu handlers expose `selectSlashItem`, `selectAgentItem`, and `handleSlashMenuKey`/`handleMentionMenuKey` with modifier-key guards.

eli5.text: When you press Ctrl+C in the CLI, the first press now clears your current input line instead of immediately trying to quit, and the second press cleanly sends your usage statistics before exiting. If your conversation grows beyond 60 messages, only the most recent ones (plus a small buffer) are kept actively loaded and rendered on screen, while older ones are tucked out of view to keep the interface responsive. The slash command and @mention menus now intercept keyboard input more precisely, so navigating them with arrow keys or selecting an item won't accidentally trigger broader app shortcuts that happen to use the same keys. ai.title: base2 prompt tweak
ai.summary: Internal prompt adjustment in base2.ts. Changed instruction from strict orchestration to helpful assistant with judgement-based sub-agent/tool use. Scope limited to .agents/base2/base2.ts. No user-facing behavior or API changes.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that helps draft messages was given a friendlier, more flexible instruction set, instead of rigidly assigning tasks to its helper tools, it can now decide thoughtfully how to answer you. This tweak is purely behind-the-scenes: nothing you click or read will look different today, and no features changed. If you peeked at the system logs, you might notice the assistant now considers your request first before choosing which helpers to wake up.

ai.title: base2 agent prompt refactor: toolresult guard added
ai.summary: Adds instruction to never write <tool_result> tags. Moves buildImplementationStepPrompt above buildPlanOnlyInstructionsPrompt in .agents/base2/base2.ts. Refactor only; no behavior change to model routing or user-facing commands.

eli5.text: The assistant will now stop writing out its own tool call results in its replies, since those results get added automatically. This is purely a behind-the-scenes cleanup of the instruction text the assistant reads before responding, so you won’t see any difference in how it answers your questions.

ai.title: Rename best-of-n editor agents to editor-best-of-n
ai.summary: Renamed internal agent IDs and files from `best-of-n-editor` to `editor-best-of-n` (and GPT-5 variants) in `.agents/base2/`. Updated `base2.ts` spawn logic and prompts, plus `base2-gpt-5-worker.ts` tool references, to match new identifiers. Files renamed: `best-of-n-editor.ts` to `editor-best-of-n.ts` and `best-of-n-editor-gpt-5.ts` to `editor-best-of-n-gpt-5.ts`. No user-facing behavior change; internal consistency fix for agent naming convention.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the internal labels used to identify certain specialized assistant tools have been flipped from 'best-of-n-editor' to 'editor-best-of-n' (with the GPT-5 variant adjusted the same way). Anyone who builds or maintains these internal tools will now see the reversed naming show up consistently in the configuration files and the instructions those tools follow when they spin up helpers. Functionally nothing behaves differently: the tools still do exactly what they did before, only the internal name has changed.

ai.title: Shorten CLI chat input placeholder
ai.summary: Input placeholder text in cli/src/chat.tsx shortened to "Enter a coding task or / for commands". Reduces visual clutter in the CLI prompt. Scope limited to cli/src/chat.tsx.

eli5.text: When you open the chat command line and the input box is empty, you'll now see a shorter hint that reads "Enter a coding task or / for commands" instead of the longer previous text. This affects anyone using the command line to interact with the assistant, making the prompt area look less crowded. You wouldn't see any change in capability, only the wording of the faint example text disappears and a briefer version takes its place in the same input box you already use.

ai.title: CLI: support system theme in JetBrains and Zed detection
ai.summary: Added logic to handle IDE theme settings configured to "system". `extractJetBrainsTheme` returns null when `LafManager` autodetect is true, and `extractZedTheme` returns null when mode is "system", triggering `detectPlatformTheme` fallback. This change affects `cli/src/utils/theme-system.ts`.

eli5.text: When your computer is set to automatically switch between light and dark themes, some code editors (like those from JetBrains and Zed) now correctly follow that system setting instead of ignoring it. Previously, the assistant would try to guess your theme preference by reading the editor's settings file, but when the file just said 'follow my system', it didn't know what to do and might pick the wrong theme. Now, when it detects that the editor is set to follow your operating system's theme, it checks your computer's actual light/dark setting and uses that instead.

ai.title: Switch base2 agents to default plan mode
ai.summary: Seven `base2` agent definitions in `.agents/base2/` now pass `'default'` to `createBase2` instead of `'fast'`. This change aligns the agent configurations with the updated plan mode default. The affected agents include `base2-alloy`, `base2-gpt-5-single-step`, `base2-alloy2`, `base2-plan-step`, `base2-plan`, `base2-read-moar`, and `base2-with-file-researcher`.

eli5.text: The assistant agents that help decide how to approach a task now take the time to think through a plan by default, instead of rushing into the first fast answer. If you've worked with these particular assistant types before, you'll notice they pause to lay out a clearer sequence of steps before acting. This only affects the specific group of assistants listed and went into effect on 2025-11-10.

ai.title: Indent base2-plan example answers
ai.summary: Added two-space indentation to example answer options in base2-plan prompt. Affects .agents/base2/base2.ts. Ensures consistent formatting for user-facing clarification prompts.

eli5.text: When you ask the internal planning assistant a multiple-choice question, the suggested answers now have a bit of extra space in front of them, so each option lines up neatly under the question instead of hugging the left edge. This only changes how those example answer options look in the prompt you never see directly; the assistant's actual advice to you stays the same.

ai.title: Add useWhyDidYouUpdateById hook to MessageBlock
ai.summary: Added `useWhyDidYouUpdateById` hook to `MessageBlock` in `cli/src/components/message-block.tsx`. This hook logs re-render reasons for debugging, currently disabled by default (`enabled: false`). Refactored `MessageBlock` to use the new hook alongside existing memoization. Scope limited to CLI component rendering logic.

eli5.text: Developers added a behind-the-scenes debugging tool to the assistant's on-screen chat interface that silently tracks why individual message boxes pop up on your screen again. The tool is turned off by default, so you won't see anything change now, but it gives the team a way to catch and fix glitches that make parts of your chat window re-render unexpectedly. If you looked at the code, you'd see this tracking helper living alongside the existing code that already stops message boxes from updating unless something actually changed. Today it sits in place doing nothing yet, waiting for someone to flip its switch when they need to hunt down a rendering bug.

ai.title: Fix SDK prompt caching provider keys
ai.summary: Prompt caching failed because `codebuff` provider key mismatched `openaiCompatible` in `withCacheControl`. Switched provider key to `openaiCompatible` and renamed `cacheControl` to `cache_control` in `common/src/util/messages.ts`. Added explicit provider routing orders for Claude models in `sdk/src/impl/llm.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask an assistant to remember earlier parts of your conversation instead of re-reading them, it stopped working for certain AI services because an internal name used to identify those services didn't match what the system expected. The fix corrects that name and the spelling of how caching settings are passed along, and it tells the system explicitly which AI services to try first when you use Claude models. If you rely on prompt caching through the supported AI providers, caching now works again instead of silently doing nothing.

ai.title: Prompt caching integration test for SDK
ai.summary: Added `sdk/src/__tests__/run.integration.test.ts` verifying prompt caching cost reduction. Test asserts second request with `previousRun` is cheaper than first. Scope limited to SDK integration tests.

eli5.text: Programmers who build on top of the CodeBuff toolkit now have an automated check that confirms a cost-saving feature really works. When the same prompt is sent twice in a row, the second pass reuses the cached portion of the earlier work, so it should bill for less. The new test sends a long prompt followed by a short follow-up and simply verifies that the second charge is smaller than the first, catching any future slip where that discount stops applying.

ai.title: Rename codebuff to openaiCompatible in messages tests
ai.summary: Tests updated to expect `openaiCompatible` provider key and `cache_control` snake_case property. Aligns assertions with production code changes renaming `codebuff` to `openaiCompatible` and standardizing cache control keys. Scope limited to `common/src/util/__tests__/messages.test.ts`. No runtime impact; ensures test suite reflects current provider option structure.

eli5.text: When you connect this software to an AI provider (like ChatGPT-style services), the way it labels that connection changed: it used to call a generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint "codebuff" and used a camelCase key "cacheControl" for caching; now it calls it "openaiCompatible" and uses "cache_control". This is purely a behind-the-scenes rename in the test files to match the new naming, so nothing the user sees or how the software behaves has changed.

ai.title: Add sdk package to CI test matrix
ai.summary: Added `sdk` to the package matrix in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for both unit and integration test jobs. Ensures SDK changes are validated in CI. No user-facing impact.

eli5.text: The project's automated testing system now also checks the SDK code whenever changes are made, just like it already did for other parts of the project. Previously, the SDK was left out of these automatic checks, so errors there could slip through unnoticed. Now, if someone makes a change to the SDK that breaks something, the build will catch it before it affects anyone. This is purely a behind-the-scenes safeguard and has no impact on what you see or do as a user.

ai.title: Add 60s timeout to CI integration tests
ai.summary: Added `--timeout=60000` to `bun test` commands in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Prevents integration tests from hanging indefinitely by enforcing a 60-second limit. Affects both `.agents` and standard package test executions.

eli5.text: Integration tests in the continuous integration pipeline now stop automatically if they take longer than 60 seconds, instead of running forever. The change affects all integration test runs, both the special tests inside the agents package and the tests inside every other package folder. If you looked at the test results page, you would see long-running tests ending sooner and failing fast, rather than spinning until someone manually canceled them.

ai.title: Fix unit tests for sdk
ai.summary: Fix unit tests for sdk. Adjust formatting in `sdk/src/run-state.ts` to resolve test failures.

eli5.text: The system that checks for mistakes in a helper tool used by developers has been repaired, so its built-in self-tests now pass reliably. The fix adjusts how the tool looks for and organizes special instruction files it relies on during testing. You would only notice this if you run the tool's automated test suite: previously some checks could fail unexpectedly, and now they complete without that error.

ai.title: Fix up/down arrow cursor movement across wrapped lines in multiline
ai.summary: MultilineInput now correctly moves cursor up/down across wrapped lines by calculating visual rows and respecting paragraph boundaries. Previous logic blindly added/subtracted effective columns, causing jumps to wrong lines when text wrapped or contained newlines. Cursor highlighting also excludes newline characters to prevent visual glitches. Affects cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx.

eli5.text: When typing a long message in the chat that wraps onto multiple lines, pressing the up or down arrow keys now moves the cursor to the matching spot on the line above or below instead of jumping to an unpredictable position. Previously, if your text wrapped on screen, the cursor would leap to the wrong line, making it hard to navigate your own message. The fix calculates where each wrapped line starts and stops, and also stops the cursor highlight from accidentally grabbing invisible line-break characters that caused visual glitches. This is already live today for anyone typing in the multiline chat input.

ai.title: Fix cursor column calculation when scrolling down through newlines
ai.summary: Corrects cursor positioning in `cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx` when navigating down across wrapped lines. The previous logic for calculating the current column relative to the last newline was flawed, causing misalignment. The fix introduces `prevNewlineExclusive` to accurately compute the column offset. This ensures the cursor lands on the correct character when moving down through soft-wrapped text.

eli5.text: When typing a long command that wraps onto multiple lines in the terminal, pressing the down arrow key could place the cursor at the wrong spot. Now it correctly jumps to the matching character on the next visible line. If you watch the cursor move while scrolling through wrapped text, it will land where you expect instead of drifting left or right.
